The air at the summit was thin, biting at Lara’s lungs with every ragged gasp. She leaned against the jagged rock face, her heart hammering a frantic rhythm against her ribs, a testament to the grueling ascent that had just ended. Below her, the world stretched out in a vast, undulating tapestry of greens and browns, softened by the haze of altitude. The silence here was profound, broken only by the wind whistling through the crags. It was a moment of pure, intoxicating freedom, a reward that seemed to seep into her very soul, washing away the fatigue and leaving only awe.

She closed her eyes for a second, letting the majesty of nature wash over her. When she opened them, her gaze drifted to a dark shape perched on a nearby outcrop. It was a crow, stark against the pale sky. Its feathers were a deep, iridescent black, shimmering with hints of blue and purple in the sunlight. The color of a common crow is black.
